question: What is the main job of a medical mask in the ward?

options.D: Providing a continuous supply of oxygen

explanation: Think of a medical mask as a friendly shield! It catches the tiny droplets that come out when people cough, talk, or sneeze, keeping everyone safe. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h1)

question: Why is wearing masks and respiratory protection extra important in a busy, crowded hospital ward?

options.A: Patients prefer healthcare workers to wear facial coverings
options.B: Hospital regulations require masks for aesthetic purposes
options.C: Air conditioning systems circulate stagnant infectious particles
options.D: Crowded wards speed up airborne and droplet pathogen transmission

explanation: When lots of people are close together in a ward, germs travel fast through the air. Masks help break that chain of transmission! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of a standard surgical mask?

options.A: Sealing completely around the chin and cheeks
options.B: Filtering out 95 percent of tiny airborne dust particles
options.C: Supplying filtered chemical-free oxygen to the lungs
options.D: Protecting the patient from the wearer's respiratory droplets

explanation: Standard surgical masks act mainly as 'source control'—they stop your own coughs and sneezes from reaching an open wound or a vulnerable patient. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h2)

question: When should you as a nurse grab a fluid-resistant mask instead of a normal procedure mask?

options.A: During procedures with a high risk of blood or fluid splatters
options.B: When entering a private room for routine vital sign checks
options.C: While charting patient notes at the nursing station desk
options.D: During routine patient bed bath and linen changes

explanation: Whenever there's a chance of blood or body fluids splashing toward your face, you want that extra fluid-resistant layer to keep yourself safe! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h2)

question: In an N95 respirator, what does the number '95' actually mean?

options.A: Can be safely worn for up to 95 consecutive hours
options.C: Filters at least 95 percent of airborne particles
options.D: Contains 95 distinct layers of protective filtration mesh

explanation: You've got this! '95' simply means the filter blocks out at least 95% of tiny test particles, giving you heavy-duty respiratory protection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h3)

question: Why must a nurse be clean-shaven to wear an N95 respirator properly?

options.A: Beards trap harmful chemicals that degrade the filter material
options.B: Facial hair prevents the mask from forming a tight seal
options.C: Stubble makes the elastic straps lose their tension quickly
options.D: Hospital infection control policies prohibit all facial hair

explanation: For an N95 to work its magic, it needs an airtight seal against your skin. Stubble or beards leave tiny gaps where unfiltered air can slip right in. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h3)

question: Which mask is a must-have when caring for a patient diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis?
explanation: TB travels easily through tiny airborne nuclei. That's why we always reach for a tightly sealed N95 respirator for protection! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h4)

question: You are caring for a patient with suspected influenza in the medical ward. What protection do you need on your face?

options.D: Full gas mask with chemical canisters

explanation: Flu spreads mainly through larger droplets, so a standard surgical mask is your reliable go-to for routine care. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h4)

question: What is the very first thing you should do before putting on a medical mask?

options.C: Tie the lower strings behind the neck
options.D: Check the expiration date on the box

explanation: Always wash or sanitize your hands first! This ensures you don't transfer any sneaky germs from your fingers onto your clean mask. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h5)

question: How do you perform a quick user seal check on your N95 respirator?

options.A: Submerging the masked face in a basin of clean water
options.B: Asking a colleague to smell perfume near the mask edges
options.C: Inhaling and exhaling sharply to check for air leaks
options.D: Stretching the elastic straps until they snap tightly

explanation: Take a sharp breath in (the mask should collapse inward slightly) and blow out (check for air escaping around the edges). If no air leaks, you're good to go! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h5)

question: When taking off a used mask, which part is safe to touch?

options.A: The center of the filter front
options.C: The ties, bands, or ear loops
options.D: The lower edge near the chin

explanation: Always handle your mask by the straps or loops. The front part has been catching germs and is considered contaminated! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h6)

question: Why is washing your hands immediately after taking off a mask so important?

options.A: To remove any pathogens that may have touched the hands during removal
options.B: To neutralize chemical residues left behind by mask manufacturing
options.C: To cool down the skin after wearing a hot facial covering
options.D: To comply with hospital paperwork and administrative checklists

explanation: Even if you're careful, your fingers might accidentally brush against the outer mask surface while removing it. A quick handwash washes those germs away! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h6)

question: Why is pulling your mask down around your neck a big infection control mistake?

options.A: It blocks the collar opening and makes breathing difficult
options.B: It transfers neck microbes onto the inner surface of the mask
options.C: It signals to patients that the nurse is unprofessional
options.D: It stretches the elastic straps beyond their functional limit

explanation: Pulling your mask down to your neck lets skin bacteria and dust onto the inside of the mask. When you pull it back up, those germs go straight into your nose and mouth! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is the risk of tossing a used disposable mask straight into your uniform pocket for later?

options.A: Body heat activates dormant chemicals inside the filter paper
options.B: The mask absorbs moisture and expands to twice its original size
options.C: The fabric of the pocket permanently stains the mask material
options.D: Pathogens accumulated on the filter transfer to the uniform and hands

explanation: Pockets are full of hidden dirt and bacteria. Storing a dirty mask there means spreading germs to your uniform, your hands, and your own pockets. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h7)
